findings.description: The bucket has no acl specified and comments confirm it is public, meaning anyone can read/write objects including sensitive customer data, with no bucket ACL restricting access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in this bucket are not encrypted at rest, risking data exposure if underlying storage is compromised.
Versioning is not enabled, so accidental or malicious deletion/overwrite of objects (including the sensitive customer-master.xlsx) cannot be recovered.

This object (customer-master.xlsx, likely containing sensitive customer data) is stored in the aws_s3_bucket.data bucket which is public and unencrypted, exposing sensitive data to unauthorized access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket holding financial data, leaving data unencrypted at rest.
Versioning is not enabled, risking permanent loss or tampering of financial records without recovery capability.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so operational data stored in this bucket is not encrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so data science datasets are stored unencrypted at rest.
